title: New to MKU? Welcome to MKU Christian Union
excerpt: Starting university can feel like stepping into a completely new world. For first-year students, visitors and anyone looking for a Christian community at Mount Kenya University, MKU Christian Union is a place to worship, grow, serve and find fellowship.
content:
Beginning university is more than joining a new class. It means learning a new environment, meeting new people, making decisions for yourself and discovering the kind of person you want to become. If you are a first-year student at Mount Kenya University, a continuing student looking for fellowship, or simply visiting us in Thika, we want you to know one thing from the beginning: there is a place for you here.

MKU Christian Union is a student Christian community at Mount Kenya University, Thika Campus. Our desire is simple: to know God, grow in Christ and live out the Gospel on campus and beyond. Our vision is to nurture a Christ-centred student community that knows God, lives out the Gospel and influences the campus and society.

More Than a Sunday Service

Church on campus is not meant to be only a place you visit once a week. Christian community becomes especially important during university life because this is a season of growth, questions, pressure, opportunity and change.

At MKU CU, students gather for worship, prayer, Scripture, discipleship, fellowship, evangelism and missions. There are opportunities throughout the week to pray together, study the Bible, build friendships and serve. Sunday brings the wider family together for corporate worship, teaching and fellowship, while smaller gatherings during the week help make a large campus feel more like home.

Find Your People

One of the biggest questions for a new student is often, Where do I belong?

You do not have to navigate campus life alone. MKU CU has home fellowships and smaller communities where students can pray, study Scripture, encourage one another and build genuine friendships. These spaces can become some of the most important relationships of your university years.

Do not wait until you know everyone before getting involved. Come as you are. Introduce yourself. Sit with someone new. Join a fellowship. Ask questions. Community grows when we choose to participate in it.

There Is a Place for Your Gift

Perhaps you sing. Perhaps you love photography, video, design or technology. Maybe you enjoy welcoming people, praying, teaching Scripture, evangelism, drama, instruments or working quietly behind the scenes. There is room to serve.

MKU CU has ministries including Praise & Worship, Intercessory Ministry, Bible Study, Missions & Evangelism, Multimedia, Creative Ministry, Choir, Ushering & Protocol, Ladies & Gents, Home Fellowships, Children's Ministry, and Sound & Instrumentalists.

Serving is not merely about filling a duty roster. It is an opportunity to discover your gifts, develop discipline, learn to work with others and use what God has placed in you for the good of His people.

Your Academic Journey Matters Too

Faith and academics do not have to compete. University is part of your stewardship. Attend your classes. Learn deeply. Build good habits. Ask for help when you need it. Make friends who encourage both your spiritual growth and your academic responsibility.

The Christian Union exists within a wider university community, and Mount Kenya University provides chaplaincy and pastoral support for students and staff. University life will have demanding seasons, but those seasons are easier to face when you are rooted in prayer, wise relationships and a healthy community.

If You Are Visiting, You Are Welcome

You do not need to understand everything about MKU CU before attending. You do not need a special invitation, and you do not need to pretend to have everything figured out. Whether you are already a Christian, exploring faith, transferring to MKU, visiting a friend or looking for a church family while studying in Thika, you are welcome to come and meet us.

Our Sunday service is normally held from 7:00 AM to 12:45 PM, with the venue communicated through the church schedule and announcements because venues can occasionally change. If it is your first time, arriving a little early gives you time to find the venue and meet the welcoming team.

Your First Few Steps

If you are new, keep it simple:

  1. Come to a Sunday service. Experience the worship, Word and fellowship for yourself.
  2. Join a home fellowship or Bible study. Smaller groups make it easier to build meaningful relationships.
  3. Explore a ministry. Find an area where your gifts and willingness can serve others.
  4. Build a prayer life. University will stretch you; stay anchored in God.
  5. Stay connected. Follow the church schedule, events, notice board and announcements so you know what is happening.

Welcome Home

Your years at university will move faster than they seem. There will be lectures and exams, victories and difficult days, friendships, decisions, growth and memories that stay with you long after graduation. In the middle of all of it, make room for God and for people who will help you walk faithfully.

MKU Christian Union is not simply another activity to add to your timetable. It is an invitation into Christian community: to worship together, learn together, pray together, serve together and carry the Gospel beyond ourselves.

Welcome to Mount Kenya University. Welcome to Thika. And welcome to the MKU CU family.

“Now this is eternal life: that they know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom you have sent.” — John 17:3
